reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Cr's role in promoting selective Al oxidation and forming Laves phases in Nb-Al alloys, and pest oxidation via grain boundary oxygen diffusion in Nb-silicide alloys, but neither passage provides direct support for Cr/Ti grain boundary segregation in the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA, nor for the formation of a protective Cr/Ti-rich scale under the proposed conditions. The key premises about segregation behavior, scale formation, and matrix stability are unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Cr and Ti can segregate to grain boundaries during heat treatment in this alloy system
Grain boundary segregation of Cr and Ti promotes formation of a continuous, adherent Cr/Ti-rich oxide scale in oxidizing conditions
This oxide scale acts as a barrier against oxygen ingress, reducing internal oxidation
In reducing atmospheres, the absence of this scale leads to increased internal oxidation and embrittlement
The fcc matrix and mechanical integrity are retained after the proposed heat treatment
